name.basis: The firm's own brand on kleinerperkins.com. Legal name Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, LLC, primary business name 'Kleiner Perkins' (Form ADV Item 1.A and 1.B, CRD 161035, signed 2026-03-31). The firm traded as Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (KPCB) until the rebrand: the last kpcb.com captures are 2018-03 and kleinerperkins.com is captured from 2018-07-17 (sources/wayback/cc-manifest-kp.json), so the archive dates the rename to 2018, while decisions.md says 'until the 2019 rebrand'; no press article dating it was found. Fund vehicles kept the long name through XIX (2020) and dropped it from Kleiner Perkins XX (2022).

founding_year.basis: Wikipedia, 'Kleiner Perkins' (scratch/wiki/Kleiner_Perkins.txt): founded in 1972 by Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins in Menlo Park. The firm's own 2026 post agrees ('For 54 years', 2026 less 54 is 1972).

investment_concept.basis: The hero headline of the firm's homepage, 'Make History' (the tagline in the hero's company ticker, and the description of the page's own WebSite schema), read 2026-09-30; set in sentence case with one closing period and published in quotation marks as the firm's own words. Competing line: the meta description, 'Kleiner Perkins is an American venture capital firm headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park in Silicon Valley.' The About page's mission also carries the phrase: 'To be the first call for founders who want to make history and to partner with them as company builders in pursuit of that goal.'

history.value: Kleiner Perkins was founded in 1972 in Menlo Park by Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins. The bets that made it were Genentech, Compaq, Sun Microsystems, Netscape, Amazon and Google, followed later by Twitter, Spotify, Slack, DoorDash and Figma. In 2026 it raised $3.5 billion: a $1 billion early-stage fund, its twenty-second, and $2.5 billion for growth investments.
history.basis: Founding (1972, Menlo Park, Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins) from Wikipedia, 'Kleiner Perkins'; the firm's 2026 post says 'For 54 years'. The bets are the firm's own company pages on kleinerperkins.com, each with its 'Partnered Since' year: Genentech 1976 (co-founded by 'a young KP partner' with the firm's seed capital), Compaq 1982 ('one of the most important bets in KP history') and Sun Microsystems 1982, Netscape 1994, Amazon 1996, Google 1999 ('We wrote our largest check ever'), Twitter 2010, Spotify 2011, Slack 2014, DoorDash 2015, Figma 2017; all eleven are verified portfolio companies. The raise is the firm's post of 2026-03-24 (https://www.kleinerperkins.com/perspectives/our-new-funds-kp22-select-iv-flex/): 'KP22, a $1 billion fund to back early-stage companies' and '$2.5 billion in growth funds', $3.5 billion in all (TechCrunch, 2026-03-24, 'With $3.5B in fresh capital, Kleiner Perkins is going all in on AI'). Moved to this sidecar, not the page: the name Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (Frank Caufield and Brook Byers became name partners; Byers joined in 1977) and the rebrand to Kleiner Perkins; the growth team under Mary Meeker, which left in September 2018 to form Bond, and the return to early-stage investing under Mamoon Hamid (joined 2017) and Ilya Fushman (joined 2018) with the $600M KP18 in January 2019; the green technology years (Green Growth Fund, 2008); KPCB China (2007, provisionally inside the portfolio on this page, decisions.md X1); the fund ladder (funds field); the firm's own count of over 1,000 companies backed and over $35 billion returned to its limited partners (post of 2022-01-11); the gross assets of its private funds (aum field).

aum.basis: Kleiner Perkins (Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, LLC; CRD 161035, SEC 802-75571) is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER, so it files no Item 5.F and no regulatory assets under management exist. The sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B.(1) of its Form ADV signed 2026-03-31 (data/filings/adv/161035.pdf, parsed into sources/adv/adv-7b-funds.json). BOTTOM: $20,693,034,506, the sum of the current gross asset values of the 42 private funds Kleiner Perkins itself reports (41 with a parsed value; KLEINER PERKINS SELECT FOUNDERS FUND III, LLC has no parsed value in that file and adds nothing, although the ADV text prints $18,659,493 beneath its name, so the floor is understated by about that much). It includes KPCB China Fund II, L.P. ($445,311,206), which is on Kleiner Perkins' own 7.B.(1). TOP: $21,051,591,900, the bottom plus the $358,557,394 that KPCB China Management, Ltd. (CRD 161470, SEC 802-75570, its own exempt reporting adviser) reports on its own 7.B.(1) for KPCB China Founders Fund, L.P. ($24,521,518) and KPCB China Fund, L.P. ($334,035,876). KPCB China is provisionally inside the firm's boundary (decisions.md X1) and both of those funds are on Kleiner Perkins' own 7.B.(2) as funds it advises that another adviser reports, so the affiliated adviser's gross assets are added for the top only (COLLECTION.md s11, the Accel London shape); no fund is counted twice, the rosters are deduplicated by private fund ID. If Erik rules KPCB China out, the top falls to the bottom (and KPCB China Fund II would leave the bottom as well). Gross asset value is not net assets and not commitments: the 2026 funds are carried at the amounts they raised (XXII $995,000,000, Select Fund IV $1,920,000,000), which reads as commitments, not invested assets. Bond Capital Management (CRD 304391) is a separate firm since 2018 and is in neither end. No press figure is used.

funds.basis: 22 funds and sleeves from 2006 on, newest first: the numbered funds XII to XXII, the Digital Growth Funds I to III, the Green Growth Fund, the Select Funds I to IV, Flex I, and KPCB China Fund and Fund II (the last two under the provisional reading of decisions.md X1). Sizes are the firm's own announcements where it made one (2020 on), press otherwise, each with its source. FILING STYLE: until 2022 the firm filed a fixed total-offering amount before first close ($0 sold) and rarely amended, and in every such case (XIV to XX, Select I and II, Digital Growth II and III, China Fund II) the offering equals the announced size to the dollar, which corroborates the size but cannot be asserted against an amount sold. From 2024 it files at close with the full amount sold, so exactly five entries carry an accession, asserted against the filing at build time: XXI, Select Fund III, XXII, Select Fund IV and Flex I. The funds before 2009 (XII, XIII, Green Growth, China Fund) filed on paper. NOT LISTED: the Founders Funds and Friends funds beside each main fund (KPCB XII to XIX Founders Fund, Kleiner Perkins XX and XXI Founders Fund, Select Founders Funds I to III, Digital Growth Founders Funds I to III, XIX to XXII Friends, Select II to IV Friends, KPCB China Founders Fund): side vehicles for the partners and their circle (XX Friends and Select II Friends both report $37,575,000 sold, a likely co-issued filing); KP Sightglass I, LLC and KP Sightglass II, LLC, which have no public description and no Form D (ADV: gross assets $70,038,106 with 3 owners and $10,000,000 with 2 owners, read as bespoke vehicles for one or two investors, an inference); the KPCB Pandemic and Bio Defense Fund ($200M, 2006, VentureBeat 2006-02-15; no longer on the ADV); the sFund (announced at $250M in 2010 with Facebook, Amazon and Zynga, TechCrunch 2010-10-21, while KPCB sFund, LLC offered $50M and reported $0 sold) and the iFund ($100M in 2008, doubled to $200M in 2010, an allocation from the main funds with no vehicle of its own); KPCB I to XI, the Java Fund, the Zaibatsu funds and KPCB Edge, which predate 2006 or were not researched. Bond's funds are another firm's (decisions.md D2).

The vector wins: the source is the square mark from the header's own inline <svg> (a.kp-site-logo, viewBox 0 0 208 19; the four paths left of the wordmark, x 0 to 19.2337), saved with a black fill as sources/site/kp-mark.svg. Dry run 2026-09-30 (scratch/icon-dry-run.png, nothing uploaded): vector, a synthesized #ffffff plate behind the bare glyph, artwork scaled 0.596 into the keyline (box 60%, radius 80%), contrast 19.7:1, ramp 0.56 px. To be uploaded at ingest with `npx tsx scripts/fetch-investor-icon.ts kleiner-perkins data/collection/investors/kleiner-perkins/sources/site/kp-mark.svg`, which replaces this value with the bucket URL.

investment_stage.basis: The firm's own two stages, Early and Growth (the 'first investment stage' of each company in its CMS: Early 341, Growth 73 of the 416 companies on the live list; sources/site/raw/stage.json), crosswalked: Early straddles Seed and Series A (decisions.md D7), Growth is Growth. The fund architecture agrees: numbered early-stage funds beside the Select and Flex growth funds; the KP19 post names seeds, Series As and 'high-inflection Series Bs', the 2026 post 'At the early stage ... At growth, we remain selective'. Reconciled with the landed entry stages over the 890 verified members: undetermined 468, Growth 198, Series A 156, Seed 68; entries dated 2019 or later: Series A 49, Growth 49, Seed 39, undetermined 14. No disagreement: all three stages appear, and the large undetermined share is the era before 2006, where the record does not give the round.

investment_geo.basis: Derived from the portfolio's headquarters, because the firm's site has no geography filter (its About page says only 'bold ideas that span industries and continents'). US 757 of the 890 verified members with a known country; China 70; Europe 24 (DE 9, GB 9, SE 2, NL 1, ES 1, NO 1, IE 1); others: CA 8, IN 8, TW 6, IL 4, SG 3, PK 2, BH 1, KR 1, ID 1, MY 1, BR 1, JP 1, TR 1, ZA 1. A region is published at 2% of those members or more. The China rows are the KPCB China desk (78 rows flagged kpcb_china), inside the portfolio only under the provisional reading of decisions.md X1, and none is recent: entries dated 2019 or later are US 136, GB 6, IL 2, PK 2, NL 1, DE 1, BH 1, IE 1, ZA 1. If Erik rules KPCB China out, 'China' leaves this field with the rows.

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 240 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 25 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN: $21.2M, the median entry round over the 196 verified members whose entry round is on a Form D (p10 $4.9M, p25 $9.3M, p75 $40.0M, p90 $72.5M), published as $21.0M. It is a round size, not a cheque size, fair only for a lead investor with high ownership, and the coverage is uneven: electronic Form D starts in 2008-09 and 37 of the 196 rounds are from 2009 alone. LOWER: the firm publishes no programme floor (KP Fellows is a student work programme with no investment; KPCB Edge, the seed programme of 2015 to 2018, is discontinued), so the p10 entry round, $4.9M, stands in, flagged. The firm states no typical cheque; the one it names is 'the $25 million check that Kleiner wrote to lead Rippling's A round in 2019 ... to that point the largest early-stage investment that Kleiner had ever made'. UPPER (press-based): the largest round the firm led in the last five years, Saronic's $1.75 billion Series D of 2026-03-31 ('The round was led by Kleiner Perkins and values the company at $9.25 billion', PR Newswire, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/saronic-closes-1-75b-series-d-at-9-25b-valuation-to-accelerate-a-new-era-of-maritime-autonomy-302729238.html; the firm's own post: 'We're proud to lead their Series D'). It is the round, not the firm's cheque, which is undisclosed: at a 10 to 15% single position the largest fund, Select Fund IV at $1.92B, supports $192M to $288M, and the whole 2026 growth pool of $2.475B supports $248M to $371M. Other led rounds read: K2 Space $500M (2026), Mind Robotics $400M (2026), Rogo $160M (2026). REJECTED: aggregator claims of $1M to $3M seed cheques and a $500K to $75M range (vcsheet.com, investormatch.pro), unconfirmed.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the verified portfolio companies to a general reader, most recognised first (COLLECTION.md s11, PRO-152), each on the firm's own list with its year: Google (1999, the Series A), Amazon (1996), Twitter (2010) and Spotify (2011), and Airbnb (2015, a growth round). Next in line, left out by the cap of five: Uber, Slack, DoorDash, Netscape, Genentech and Figma; the history names most of them.

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 2750 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA (KLEINER PERKINS, CRD 161035, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31). The firm's site names no office in its served pages (2 checked), so the Form ADV stands. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.

flags.note: Both ends are sworn gross asset values of an exempt reporting adviser, not regulatory assets under management. The top adds KPCB China Management's own two funds and stands only while decisions.md X1 (KPCB China provisionally inside the firm) stands. One fund, Kleiner Perkins Select Founders Fund III, has no parsed value in sources/adv/adv-7b-funds.json.
'China' rests on the KPCB China desk (provisional, decisions.md X1) and on no entry since 2019.

The firm's own sector tags sit on 342 of the 890 portfolio rows (the live list only), crosswalked: Consumer & Marketplaces 70, AI & Applied AI 70, Healthcare & Bio 53, Industrial & Robotics 34, Fintech & Payments 13; left unmapped on purpose: Enterprise 179. Published at 25 companies or more, so Fintech & Payments stays below the line although the firm names fintech in its 2024 post ('enterprise software, consumer, healthcare, fintech and hardtech'). DISAGREEMENT, flagged and not overwritten (COLLECTION.md s11): the firm's largest sector, Enterprise, names no single value of the closed taxonomy, and the site has no Security and no Crypto sector although the portfolio holds security companies (the Lightspeed signal). The per-company focus over the verified members reads: Healthcare & Bio 157, Consumer & Marketplaces 139, Data Infrastructure 93, Industrial & Robotics 90, Climate & Energy 79, Media, Gaming & Advertising 78, SaaS 76, Fintech & Payments 54, AI & Applied AI 53, Security 44, DevTools & APIs 18, Crypto & Web3 7. Generalist: no sector carries the portfolio.

The ceiling is a round size from a press release ($1.75B, Saronic), far above what the funds support as a single cheque ($192M to $371M at 10 to 15%); the median is a Form D round-size proxy weighted to 2009 to 2016; the lower limit is the p10 of that distribution, not a stated floor.

KPCB XIII is published at the $700M of the 2008 announcement; TechCrunch 2012 says its offering was $950M, and the paper filing cannot settle it. XIV, XVI, Digital Growth Fund II and China Fund II carry their filed offering, not an announced close. XXII is published at the filed $995M, which the firm rounds to $1 billion (the history uses the firm's figure).
The rebrand from KPCB to Kleiner Perkins dates to 2018 on the archive, 2019 in decisions.md; the history names no year.
